chunks: Regarding the man with sexual impurity (junub) who washes (performs ghusl), and some of the water splashes back into the vessel. So he said:
'There is no problem. (Allah) has not laid upon you a hardship in the Religion [22:78].'

key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: vessel — the container holding the water used for ghusl
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: junub — one in a state of major ritual impurity (janaba) requiring ghusl, typically after sexual intercourse or seminal emission
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: haraj — hardship, constriction; the removal of haraj is a key principle in Islamic fiqh (nafy al-haraj)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: la ba'sa — 'there is no problem / no objection', a standard jurisprudential phrase of permissibility
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: ghusl — the full-body ritual washing to remove major ritual impurity (janaba)
key_terms.يَنْتَضِحُ: splashes back — water that bounces off the body during washing and returns to the water vessel

ai.seo_question: Is water that splashes back into the vessel during ghusl for janaba considered impure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq rules that water that splashes back into the vessel during the ghusl of someone in a state of janaba (major ritual impurity) does not contaminate the vessel, and there is no legal issue with it. The Imam grounds this ruling in the Quranic principle of ease in religion (Quran 22:78: 'He has not laid upon you a hardship in the Religion'), invoking a foundational principle of Islamic jurisprudence known as 'nafy al-haraj' (removal of hardship). This hadith established a precedent that incidental contact of wash water with the source vessel in such circumstances is excused.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the man with sexually impurity washing, and some of the water spills over into the vessel. So he<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘There is no problem. (Allahazwj) [22:78] has not Laid upon you a hardship in the Religion’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i ibn ‘Abd Allah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “It is about a man who takes Ghusl (bath) due to sexual matters and water drops sprinkle into the water container.
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not harmful. Allah has not sanctioned anything in religion which causes hardships for you.”’
